strengths: AutoSeg addresses a useful problem: generating segmentation categories automatically without runtime vocabulary specification or additional weight training. Decoding clustered BLIP patch features is a practical approach to recovering objects overlooked by whole-image captioning.

Experiments cover four diverse datasets and include useful captioning and segmentation baselines. Table 1 provides evidence independent of semantic label mapping: BBoost improves class-agnostic mIoU over BLIP + X-Decoder on every dataset, including 38.0 to 71.8 on VOC.

LAVE addresses the genuine difficulty of comparing generated categories with fixed annotations. Its aggregate results are close to manual mappings across all four datasets. The supplement supplies prompts, pseudocode, additional ablations, and informative failure cases, while the principal datasets and model dependencies are acknowledged.
weaknesses: The proposed evaluator needs stronger validation. Section 9.3 relies on the LLM remembering the PASCAL Context and ADE20K taxonomies instead of supplying their classes. Its prompts also instruct the model to map stuff to background, potentially mishandling nonexact stuff labels in datasets that explicitly annotate them. Close aggregate scores against manual mappings are encouraging but do not establish correspondence accuracy or robustness to these choices.

The separation between tuning and evaluation is unclear. Section 5.1 optimizes parameters against VOC mIoU without identifying a disjoint tuning split, while the reported datasets are validation sets. Main results also use dataset-specific best captioning counts from Table 2. A clearly held-out selection protocol and variability across stochastic runs are needed to substantiate the generalization claims.

Comparability with ZeroSeg is insufficiently documented. Tables 3–4 do not establish whether its predictions were reevaluated with the same mapper and background conventions. This matters because Table A7 shows that changing only the mapper alters VOC performance by 9.6–13.2 points. The reported PASCAL Context advantage, 11.7 versus 11.4, is particularly difficult to interpret without a shared protocol and uncertainty estimates.

The central claim of accurate open-ended recognition is supported mainly by selected visualizations. Mapping predictions back into fixed categories cannot verify their finer semantic distinctions, and generating more distinct nouns does not establish correctness or coverage. An independently annotated subset measuring generated-label correctness and corresponding mask quality would provide substantially stronger evidence.

Task novelty is overstated: the manuscript itself identifies ZeroSeg [32], published at ICCV 2023, as addressing essentially the same guidance-free setting. The defensible novelty lies in BBoost's specific local-captioning procedure and the proposed evaluator, rather than introducing segmentation without a supplied vocabulary.

Several inconsistencies hinder reproduction. Section 3.1 describes Hungarian matching, whereas Equation 9 specifies independent maximum-IoU assignments; alignment between the 24×24 and 32×32 grids is not explained. Table A6 claims one captioning cycle yields 87.1 VOC mIoU, while Table 2 reports 85.3 for one cycle and 87.1 for ten. These require clarification, and runtime measurements are missing despite the scalability motivation and repeated caption generation.
